_note: Retreat planning checklist. Each task is a card for a Notion board: title, phase, workstream, owner, essential, steps (the card checklist), deliverable, folder, done when, tools and topic links.
title: Retreat planning checklist
lead: Every task to do or consider for a training retreat, in order, from the first conversation to the ninety-day check. Open a card for its steps, what it produces, how you know it is done and the tools you need.

phases.name: Set up once
phases.when: Before your first retreat, then review each year
phases.note: Not repeated for every retreat. Do these once and keep them up to date.

phases.name: Arrive and set up
phases.when: The day before, and the first morning

tasks.title: Arrange business insurance
tasks.why: Venues, clients and activity providers will ask for it.
steps: Check outdoor and movement activities are covered
Note the renewal date in your calendar
tasks.done: Certificates saved, and the cover matches every kind of activity you run.

tasks.title: Write your standard terms
tasks.why: One set of terms you adapt for each client, instead of starting again.
steps: Scope and what is not included
Fees and payment schedule, including deposit
Have a legal professional review it
tasks.done: A legal professional has reviewed it and it is saved as a template.

tasks.title: Build your retreat templates
tasks.why: Copying a ready folder and board saves a day on every retreat.
steps: Google Drive folder with the seven numbered folders used on this page
Templates for the brief, budget, attendee list, run sheet and incident log
tasks.done: You can set up a new retreat in under five minutes.

tasks.title: Build your supplier list
tasks.why: Vetted venues and suppliers you can call on quickly.
steps: Venues you have visited, with notes
Transport, catering extras, activity providers, photographers
Insurance and qualifications checked for each
tasks.done: At least two options in each category, each checked.

tasks.title: Check your employment contract
tasks.why: If you are employed, outside work may need permission.
steps: Outside work and conflicts of interest
tasks.done: You know what you can do, and have permission in writing if needed.

tasks.title: Hold the discovery call
tasks.why: Understand the request before anyone talks about venues.
steps: Why now, and what prompted it
Who will attend, and who decides
tasks.done: The client has replied to confirm your summary.

tasks.title: Interview the sponsor and attendees
tasks.why: Find out what the retreat is really for, not only what was asked for.
steps: Two to four attendees, about 20 minutes each
Ask what success looks like, what worries them, what the team avoids
tasks.done: You can write the purpose in one sentence and the sponsor agrees with it.

tasks.title: Test whether a retreat is right
tasks.why: Going away is expensive. Make sure it beats the alternatives.
steps: Compare with a day in the office or a series of sessions
Give the sponsor your recommendation and why
tasks.done: The decision and the reason are written in the brief.

tasks.title: Set objectives and success measures
tasks.why: You cannot design or evaluate without them.
steps: Three to five objectives you could observe
Two or three changes you would see at work
Where the evidence for each will come from
The baseline you need before the retreat
tasks.done: The sponsor has agreed them in writing.

tasks.title: Profile the group
tasks.why: Who is coming shapes every design choice.
steps: How well they know each other, and any tension
Languages, and needs you already know about
tasks.done: You can describe the group in a paragraph and the sponsor recognises it.

tasks.title: Choose format, length and season
tasks.why: These decide the venue search and the budget.
steps: Residential or day-based, and how many nights
What sits before and after the event
Clashes: school holidays, year end, religious festivals
Travel: a place most people can reach by train
tasks.done: The sponsor has chosen a format and a date window.

tasks.title: Set the budget envelope
tasks.why: Agree the total before you look at venues.
steps: Your fees and any other staff
Contingency of about ten per cent
tasks.done: The sponsor has agreed the total.

tasks.title: Write the retreat brief
tasks.why: One page everyone works from.
tasks.done: The sponsor has signed it off in writing.

tasks.title: Cost and price the retreat
tasks.why: Price it so it still works if costs rise.
steps: Cost every line from the budget outline
Test it: does it still work if costs rise by ten per cent?
tasks.done: You have a price you would accept even if costs rise.

tasks.title: Send the proposal
tasks.why: Make it easy for the client to say yes.
steps: The situation in the client's words
What you will do, before, during and after
What you need from the client
tasks.done: The client has accepted it in writing.

tasks.title: Sign terms and get a purchase order
tasks.why: Large clients cannot pay without a purchase order.
steps: Send your terms, adapted for this retreat
Ask for the purchase order number
tasks.deliverable: Signed terms, purchase order, deposit invoice
tasks.done: Terms signed, purchase order number saved, deposit paid.

tasks.title: Shortlist and visit venues
tasks.why: See the rooms at the time of day you will use them.
steps: Score venues on rooms, outdoor space, access, food, quiet, bedrooms and travel
Check step-free routes, fire exits and a wet-weather space
Ask for their risk assessment and insurance
tasks.done: The client has chosen a venue.

tasks.title: Contract the venue
tasks.why: The venue contract carries most of the money and the risk.
steps: Agree who signs: you or the client
Minimum numbers and the final-numbers deadline
Have it checked if the sums are large
tasks.done: Contract signed, deposit paid, and every deadline added to the tracker.

tasks.title: Book the facilitation team
tasks.why: Book people early. Good facilitators fill their diaries.
steps: Anyone for wellbeing, movement or outdoor sessions
tasks.done: Everyone has confirmed in writing.

tasks.title: Book other suppliers
tasks.why: Transport, activities and extras.
steps: Check insurance, qualifications and risk assessments for each
tasks.done: Every supplier has confirmed in writing, with documents saved.

tasks.title: Set up the project
tasks.why: One place for everything, shared with the client.
steps: Copy the folder and board templates
Share the folder with the client lead
List who decides and who does what
Book a weekly or fortnightly check-in
tasks.done: The client has access and the first check-in is in the diary.

tasks.title: Send the save-the-date
tasks.why: Get the dates into diaries before they fill.
steps: From the sponsor, not from you
Include travel time and the follow-up session
tasks.done: Every attendee has the dates in their calendar.

tasks.title: Plan the personal data
tasks.why: Decide what you collect before you collect it.
steps: Where it is kept (the restricted folder)
A short privacy note for attendees
tasks.done: The note is written and the deletion date is in the tracker.

tasks.title: Confirm the insurance covers this retreat
tasks.why: Each retreat may add activities or places your cover does not include.
tasks.done: You have confirmed cover for every activity on this retreat.

tasks.title: Design the before, during and after
tasks.why: The retreat is the middle of a programme, not the whole of it.
steps: The follow-up sessions and reminders after, with dates
tasks.done: Every part has a date and an owner.

tasks.title: Draft the timetable
tasks.why: The shape of the days decides how much people take in.
steps: Hardest work when energy is highest
An indoor version of every outdoor slot
Nothing intense after dinner, and a clear end each day
Absorption over intensity: fewer, deeper sessions
tasks.done: The sponsor has agreed it.

tasks.title: Write the session plans
tasks.why: A plan for every slot means anyone on the team could run it.
steps: What to cut if time runs short
tasks.done: Every slot in the timetable has a plan.

tasks.title: Plan outdoor, movement and reflection time
tasks.why: Use the setting on purpose.
steps: Outdoor sessions with a reason, and a wet-weather plan
tasks.done: Each has a purpose, a slot and a fallback.

tasks.title: Plan the evenings
tasks.why: Evenings shape the mood and the risks.
steps: Optional, with a clear end time for anything organised
Something other than the bar: food, a fire, a walk, a game
tasks.done: The sponsor has agreed the rules, and they are in the joining instructions.

tasks.title: Agree phone and work-contact rules
tasks.why: Agree with the sponsor so people believe they can switch off.
steps: When people can check in with work
tasks.done: The sponsor has agreed them, and they are in the joining instructions.

tasks.title: Design for everyone
tasks.why: Check the design works for the whole group, not the typical person.
steps: A version for people who cannot stay overnight
Access needs in rooms, routes and activities
Different minds: quiet space, clear instructions, choice
tasks.done: Each known need has an answer in the plan.

tasks.title: Plan the groups and rooms
tasks.why: Who sits and works with whom changes what people learn.
steps: Mix people who rarely work together
tasks.done: Lists are ready for the run sheet and the venue.

tasks.title: Plan the evaluation
tasks.why: Decide now what you will measure, or you will not have a baseline.
steps: The feedback form for the last session
tasks.done: Forms are built and dates are in the tracker.

tasks.title: Agree how decisions get made
tasks.why: For a working offsite: avoid ideas that go nowhere.
steps: What happens to ideas that are not chosen
tasks.done: The leader has agreed them before the day.

tasks.title: Make the materials
tasks.why: Everything people see, hold or take away.
tasks.done: Everything is proofread and on the print list.

tasks.title: Write the manager briefing
tasks.why: Managers make or break what happens back at work.
steps: Why this retreat, in two lines
What to ask in week one and month one
tasks.done: The client has approved it, ready to send.

tasks.title: Get the design signed off
tasks.why: Freeze the design so you can prepare.
steps: Walk the sponsor through the timetable and plans
Agree a date after which changes need your agreement
tasks.done: The sponsor has approved it in writing.

tasks.title: Run a pre-mortem
tasks.why: Imagine it went badly, and fix the likely causes now.
steps: List why it might go badly
Change the design or add a plan for each
tasks.done: The top three risks each have a response.

tasks.title: Rehearse the hard sessions
tasks.why: Timings and hand-overs go wrong when untested.
steps: Run the trickiest sessions with the team
tasks.done: The team has run through every session that is new or high-stakes.

tasks.title: Write the duty-of-care plan
tasks.why: Write it first, so the design fits around it.
steps: What people are told in advance
Consent and the right to opt out
Who to call, and who is in charge
tasks.done: The client and the team have read it.

tasks.title: Complete the risk assessment
tasks.why: Covers every activity, the venue, travel and the outdoors.
steps: Hazards, who could be harmed and how
What you will do about each
tasks.done: Done, signed, and reviewed since the last change.

tasks.title: Write the incident plan
tasks.why: Everyone knows what to do when something goes wrong.
steps: First aider, nearest hospital and pharmacy
How to escalate, and to whom at the client
tasks.done: Every team member knows their role in it.

tasks.title: Run registration
tasks.why: One form gives you the attendee list and everyone's needs.
steps: Chase people who have not replied
tasks.done: Every attendee has replied.

tasks.title: Send the joining instructions
tasks.why: People arrive calmer when they know what to expect.
steps: Purpose and an outline of the days
What to bring, including for the weather
Describe it honestly: promise the conditions, not a transformation
tasks.done: Sent to every attendee.

tasks.title: Brief the team and suppliers
tasks.why: Everyone you bring in shares the purpose and the rules.
steps: The rules, the duty-of-care plan and the incident plan
tasks.done: Each person has confirmed they have read it.

tasks.title: Arrange travel and transfers
tasks.why: Travel is where most things go wrong on the day.
steps: Travel for the team and kit
tasks.done: Everyone knows how they are getting there.

tasks.title: Collect the baseline
tasks.why: Without a before, you cannot show an after.
steps: Send the baseline survey or pull the data
tasks.done: You have the baseline for each measure.

tasks.title: Send the pre-work
tasks.why: Short, useful and used on day one.
steps: Say how it will be used
tasks.done: Sent, with a reminder scheduled.

tasks.title: Confirm final numbers with the venue
tasks.why: The contract sets a deadline. Miss it and you pay for empty places.
tasks.done: The venue has confirmed them in writing before the deadline.

tasks.title: Send the venue the full brief
tasks.why: The venue team can only deliver what they know about.
tasks.done: The venue lead has confirmed it.

tasks.title: Write the run sheet
tasks.why: Minute by minute, so nobody has to ask.
steps: Each slot: time, what, who, where, kit
Share it with the team and the venue
tasks.done: The team and the venue have the final version.

tasks.title: Hold the team briefing
tasks.why: Walk through the days together before you arrive.
steps: Who is on call out of hours
tasks.done: Everyone has attended or watched the recording.

tasks.title: Print and pack
tasks.why: Pack against a list, not from memory.
steps: Run sheets, contact sheet and incident log
Pens, flipchart paper, tape, extension leads, speaker
Weather kit and a spare first aid kit
tasks.done: Every item on the kit list is ticked.

tasks.title: Prompt the manager conversations
tasks.why: Managers send people with a reason to use what they learn.
tasks.done: Every manager has had the briefing.

tasks.title: Do a final check with the sponsor
tasks.why: Things change in the weeks before.
steps: Changes in the business or the group
Anyone new, or anyone dropping out
A daily check-in time on site
tasks.done: Any changes are in the plan and the run sheet.

tasks.title: Send the final reminder
tasks.why: A week before: the details people forget.
steps: Who to contact on the day
tasks.done: Sent to every attendee.

tasks.title: Check the weather plan
tasks.why: Decide early which outdoor sessions move inside.
steps: Switch to indoor versions where needed
tasks.done: The run sheet shows which version of each outdoor slot you will run.

tasks.title: Walk the venue
tasks.why: Know the building before the group does.
tasks.done: You could guide someone to any space and out in an emergency.

tasks.title: Meet the venue lead
tasks.why: One conversation saves many on the day.
steps: Who to call, day and night
tasks.done: You have the venue lead's number and they have the run sheet.

tasks.title: Set up the rooms and technology
tasks.why: Set up the night before if you can.
steps: A plan that needs no technology
tasks.done: The first session could start now.

tasks.title: Set up the welcome
tasks.why: The first ten minutes set the tone.
steps: Welcome desk, badges and room keys
Incident log and contact sheet in place
tasks.done: Ready before the first person arrives.

tasks.title: Open the retreat
tasks.why: Mark the start, and give people what they need to settle.
tasks.done: Everyone knows the purpose, the rules and where things are.

tasks.title: Run the daily check-ins
tasks.why: Small adjustments each day keep the retreat on track.
steps: Team, morning and evening: energy, concerns, changes
Cut or move sessions rather than run over
tasks.done: Each day ends with an agreed plan for tomorrow.

tasks.title: Capture the outputs every day
tasks.why: Flipcharts get lost and memories fade.
steps: Upload to the folder each evening
tasks.done: Each day's outputs are in the folder by the end of the evening.

tasks.title: Look after people
tasks.why: Duty of care runs all day and all evening.
steps: Make sure people leaving early miss nothing that matters
tasks.done: Every incident is logged with what was done.

tasks.title: Close the retreat
tasks.why: Mark the end and send people back with a plan.
steps: Each person writes what they will do in week one
tasks.done: Every attendee has a plan and has filled in the form.

tasks.title: Pack down and check out
tasks.why: Leave nothing behind and no surprises on the bill.
steps: Walk the rooms with the venue for damage
Agree any extra charges before you leave
tasks.done: Rooms are clear and the venue has agreed the final charges.

tasks.title: Send the write-up
tasks.why: Within 48 hours, while it is fresh.
tasks.done: Sent to the sponsor and attendees within 48 hours.

tasks.title: Send people their plans and resources
tasks.why: Their own words, back in their inbox, a week later.
tasks.done: Sent to every attendee.

tasks.title: Brief managers for week one
tasks.why: The first week back decides what sticks.
steps: Two questions to ask in week one
tasks.done: Every manager has the questions.

tasks.title: Debrief the team
tasks.why: Learn while it is fresh.
tasks.done: Notes saved with actions.

tasks.title: Hold the wash-up with the sponsor
tasks.why: Agree what happened and what comes next.
steps: What worked and what to change
tasks.done: The sponsor has the summary and you agreed next steps.

tasks.title: Close any incidents
tasks.why: Nothing left hanging.
steps: Report to the client where needed
tasks.done: Every logged incident is closed.

tasks.title: Reconcile costs and invoice
tasks.why: Check the venue bill against the contract before you pay.
steps: Record actual costs against the budget
tasks.done: Suppliers paid, invoice sent, and your actual margin worked out.

tasks.title: Thank everyone
tasks.why: Venues and suppliers remember who thanked them.
tasks.done: Thanks sent.

tasks.title: Send the spaced reminders
tasks.why: A recall question at one and three weeks keeps it alive.
steps: One question to answer from memory
One prompt to use the skill this week
tasks.done: Both reminders sent.

tasks.title: Run the follow-up session
tasks.why: What has been tried, and what got in the way.
steps: Solve what got in the way
tasks.done: Session run and notes saved.

tasks.title: Measure the change
tasks.why: Compare with the baseline.
steps: Talk to the most and least successful attendees
Note what helped and what blocked
tasks.done: You have before and after for each measure.

tasks.title: Report results to the sponsor
tasks.why: Short, in their terms.
steps: What you would do next time
tasks.done: The sponsor has read it and you have discussed it.

tasks.title: Propose the next step
tasks.why: Good results open the next piece of work.
steps: What the client should do next
tasks.done: Sent, or agreed that none is needed.

tasks.title: Close out and hand over
tasks.why: A clean end protects you and the client.
steps: What the client keeps and who owns what next
tasks.done: The client has confirmed close-out and the folder is archived.

tasks.title: Delete the personal data
tasks.why: On the date you set at the start.
tasks.done: Deleted, and the date recorded.

tasks.title: Gather a case study
tasks.why: Stories of real change sell the next retreat.
steps: Ask the sponsor and one or two attendees
Get written consent for how it is used
tasks.done: Written and approved by the people in it.

tasks.title: Run your own retrospective
tasks.why: Improve the templates for next time.
steps: What to add or change in this checklist
Update the templates and supplier list
tasks.done: The templates and checklist have been updated.
